resources.string: On: the screen looks like e-ink paper.

Paper mode works through Android\'s own display settings (greyscale, Night Light, Extra dim), so it costs no CPU or battery. Changing them needs a permission only a computer can grant, once. With USB debugging on, run:
No computer? On the phone itself, Wireless debugging plus an app like Shizuku or LADB can run the same command. It survives reboots and app updates.
Tints the grey with Night Light, from neutral to sepia. Neutral leaves Night Light alone.
Uses Extra dim to take the glow off white, so it reads as paper rather than a light.
High-contrast text: solid black type, like e-ink.
Screens change in one step, the way e-ink does. Also makes the phone feel faster.
When a new screen opens, it flashes black and white first, like an e-ink full refresh. Turns on PaperScreen\'s accessibility service, which only listens for screen changes.
Toggle from the Quick Settings tile (long-press it for this page), or long-press the app icon for a Toggle shortcut you can also pin to the home screen.
The tile is already in Quick Settings
Turning paper mode off puts back every system setting it changed, exactly as it was. Nothing keeps running in the background.
Flashes the screen like e-ink when a new screen opens.
Listens only for which screen is open, to flash when it changes. It never reads what\'s on screen.
